title: The Power of Focus — Hebrews 12:2
paragraphs: The Power of Focus — Hebrews 12:2
He wasn’t distracted by the cross.
He looked through it.
“Fixing our eyes on Jesus…” — Hebrews 12:2
That is the power of focus.

Not pretending pain is small.
Not denying the weight.
Not calling suffering easy.

Jesus saw the shame.
Jesus felt the agony.
Jesus knew the nails were coming.
And still—He stayed locked in on the joy set before Him.

That means holy focus is not blindness.
It is obedience with tears in your eyes.
It is saying, “This hurts, but my eyes are still on Christ.”

Some of us are losing battles not because we are weak—
but because we are scattered.

Too many voices.
Too many cravings.
Too many fears.
Too many things pulling the heart away from the One who matters most.
But here’s what we miss:
Focus is spiritual warfare.

When your eyes drift, your strength drains.
When your heart chases everything, your peace fractures.
When Christ is blurred, temptation gets louder.

Hebrews 12:2 does not tell us to fix our eyes on success.
Not on people.
Not on platforms.
Not even on ourselves.
It says: fix your eyes on Jesus.
Why?

Because He is not only our example.
He is our Savior.

We were the distracted ones.
We were the wandering ones.
We were the sinners who traded eternal glory for temporary pleasure.

But Jesus stayed focused all the way to Calvary.
He endured the cross for our redemption.
He took our sin.
He bore our shame.
He rose in victory.
And now He gives grace to every heart that turns back to Him.
So today, breathe deep.

Look up.
Look again.
Look longer.

The power is not in your willpower.
The power is in the Christ you behold.

Fix your eyes on Him—
and the things trying to master you will start losing their grip.
